QUESTION 1: HOW DID THE POLICY OF CONTAINMENT CONTRIBUTE TO COLD WAR TENSIONS BETWEEN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA AND THE SOVIET UNION IN 1947?

list items.content: Study Sources 1A, 1B, 1C and 1D and answer the questions that follow.
1.1 Use Source 1A.

kids.content: Who, according to source, did Churchill blame for, 'A shadow (that) has fallen upon the scenes so lately lighted by the Allied victory'? Give TWO responses. (2 x 1)
Why do you think Churchill adopted a conciliatory (soft) attitude towards the Soviet Union despite its expansive tendencies? (1 x 2)
Define the term Iron Curtain in your own words. (1 x 2)
Comment on what Churchill implied by the words, '… all these famous cities and the populations around them lie in what I must call the Soviet sphere …' (1 x 2)
Explain the reliability of this source to a historian researching about the origins of the Cold War. (2 x 2)

(a) A bear/wolf labelled 'COMMUNIST INFILTRATION AND DICTATORSHIP THREATS' (1 x 2)

kids.content: Comment on why you would consider the caption 'WHAT WE'RE DRIVING AT' appropriate. (1 x 2)

list items.content: 1.3 Refer to Sources 1A and 1B. Explain how the information in Source 1A supports the evidence in Source 1B regarding the increasing threat of communism. (2 x 2) (4)

kids.content: What, according to the source, was the first concern of the Marshall Plan policymakers? (1 x 2)

QUESTION 2: WHY DID THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA (USA) BECOME INVOLVED IN THE ANGOLAN CIVIL WAR FROM 1975?

list items.content: QUESTION 3: HOW DID THE NON-VIOLENT APPROACH ADOPTED BY MARTIN LUTHER KING JR CHARACTERISE THE CIVIL SOCIETY PROTESTS IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA (USA) DURING THE 1960s?
Study Sources 3A, 3B, 3C and 3D and answer the questions that follow.
3.1 Refer to Source 3A.

kids.content: Who, according to the source, indirectly influenced King Jr to apply the non-violent approach to the specific problems of African Americans? (1 x 1)

Define the term non-violent mass protests in your own words.
Explain what King Jr implied by the statement, 'It (non-violence) meant putting oneself in the face of violence …', in the context of the civil society protests. (2 x 2)
What, according to the source, did King Jr want to achieve by organising thousands across the South in specific mass actions?

list items.content: 3.2 Read Source 3B.

kids.content: According to the source, why did King Jr believe that the point of making a choice among militant, massive non-violence or riots had arrived? Give TWO responses. (2 x 1)
What did King Jr imply by the words, 'But I am convinced that if rioting continues, it will strengthen the right wing of the country …'?
Give any TWO reasons in the source suggesting that King Jr was totally committed to the non-violent approach. (2 x 1)
Explain the term racial justice in the context of the USA in the 1960s. (1 x 2)
Comment on the usefulness of this source for a historian researching non-violent protest in the USA in the 1960s. (2 x 2)
